summary: Attacked part 2 of the Modular and automorphic forms area — AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights, AutomorphicBundles, HabiroNahmSeries, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves, OverconvergentAutomorphicForms, PadicFamilies, QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms: 8 roadmaps, 79 stages, 20 accepted paper routes. One finding, medium: Shimura's bounded-denominators theorem is stated by no node, although R15.2's decomposition imports it and a second roadmap records that it has no supplier. Four apparent findings dissolved on calibration, one of them a phantom created by my own indexer, and the bookkeeping heads are clean — every roadmap with an empty consumers list is a genuine sink, and the atlas's entire stage-edge graph resolves.
checked: All 79 stages of the eight roadmaps — ModularForms 16, HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves 13, HabiroNahmSeries 11, AutomorphicBundles 9, OverconvergentAutomorphicForms 9, PadicFamilies 8, QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms 7, AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights 6 — with their descriptions, dependencies and audit verdicts: 61 not built, 12 partly built, 1 built, 1 process, 4 unaudited.

Eligibility, measured rather than assumed, and one job declined. Part 1 of this area (issue #1491) is not eligible for me: PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23 routes to three of its eight roadmaps and I authored content in that extraction rather than merely reviewing it, so its route reasons could not serve as my evidence. I skipped it and took part 2, whose eight roadmaps receive no route from any paper I have written or reviewed — checked at route granularity across all 207 paper result files.

All 20 route reasons in full. 20 routes across 79 stages is thin — a quarter of the density of the Function fields area — so the omissions head had much less to work with than in that area, and I say so rather than presenting a thin pass as a clean one.

Dependency bookkeeping, with a sink check on each roadmap declaring no consumers. All three are genuine sinks or correct: OverconvergentAutomorphicForms is cited by exactly the ten roadmaps it declares as prerequisites; QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms by exactly its seven; and HabiroNahmSeries is cited by five, of which the single one that is not among its prerequisites is ArithmeticQuantumTopology, which is precisely what it declares as its one consumer. For every roadmap the cross-roadmap stage `requires` edges are contained in the declared prerequisites.

The opaque-handle test, promoted to a standing check after it produced a high-severity finding in RT-AREA-arithmeticgeometry-3, and it comes back clean here for a reason worth recording. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms contains fourteen references of the form #NN and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights one, but reading them shows they are not roadmap references: ModularForms' are its own internal item numbers — 'Eisenstein series with character (#37)', 'The coefficient field ... of a newform (#34)', 'Hecke characteristic polynomials (#35)', 'Satake parameters and angles (#32)', 'Inner twists (#42)', 'Labels (#33, #13)', 'Bad primes (#54)' — and its one genuine cross-roadmap reference names the roadmap as well as the number, 'the consumer is the automorphic-representations roadmap, TauCetiRoadmap PR #120'. The single #81 in AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights sits inside a stageEdge title inherited from ModularCurvesPartII, 'Integral coarse spaces and comparison with #81', so it is the same defect already filed in RT-AREA-arithmeticgeometry-3 rather than a new one, and that roadmap does declare ModularCurvesPartII as a prerequisite. This does refine the earlier finding: #NN in the atlas is ambiguous between an internal item number and a pull-request number, which is part of why the ModularCurves dependency was hard to see.

A phantom finding produced by my own indexer, recorded because it is the fifth of this kind in this session and the most nearly filed. Two roadmaps here have stage `requires` entries of the form UPSTREAM:X that are not in their prerequisites — HabiroNahmSeries:HB.5a requires 'UPSTREAM:ModularForms-finite-index-subgroups' and QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.6 requires 'UPSTREAM:RepresentationTheory'. Calibration dissolves it: UPSTREAM: is an atlas-wide convention for an upstream dependency that is not an atlas stage, used by 29 roadmap files with more than 25 distinct targets (UPSTREAM:ECD 48 times, UPSTREAM:CohomologicalPointCounting 42), and in both cases here the roadmap does declare the corresponding roadmap at prerequisite level. Then a broader sweep appeared to show 85 `requires` targets resolving to no stage, including MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.0 to LV.5 and AnalyticStacks:AS.4 — which would have been a serious dangling-reference finding. It was my indexer: those files store stage keys bare (key 'LV.0', id null) while references use the qualified form, exactly the trap I recorded when red-teaming the AdicSpaces link map. Indexing both forms, 8610 identifiers in all, leaves zero non-UPSTREAM requires targets unresolved. The atlas's stage-edge graph resolves completely.

Audit coverage, where HabiroNahmSeries has 4 of its 11 stages absent from the accepted audit (KU-admissibility, KU-habiromembership, KU-nahmasymptotic, KU-nahmtorsion). Calibration shows this is within norms and not a finding: 1316 of 1962 atlas stages are audited (67 per cent), and of 210 roadmaps 125 are fully audited, 21 partially and 64 not audited at all. A partially audited roadmap sits in a small but populated class, and audits are separate jobs.

The library boundary. 61 of 79 stages are audited `not built`; the 12 partly built and 1 built are concentrated in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms (8 partly, 1 built), which is the classical end of the area. No stage instructs construction of something an audit records as built, and ModularForms is explicit about consuming what exists, marking material already in the library as such — for instance noting of the coefficient field that 'This is already constructed and proved in AINTLIB'.

Two further routes whose phrasing looked like a gap and is not. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's route says the proof of its Lemma 8.14 'uses such a formula without citation' — but the formula in question is one R15.3 is already instructed to construct ('Construct the Hasse invariant, Frobenius/Verschiebung and theta operator with their q-expansion formulas and Hecke compatibilities'), so the missing citation is the paper's, not the atlas's. PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-VENTULLO-18 routes 'three facts about Hida families over a totally real field that the paper uses without proof' to L5, which owns the Hida control theorem on integral Hilbert automorphic modules over totally real fields, so they land inside a stated target.

PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25's four part-ii routes, which raise unowned material through the programme's own mechanism rather than leaving it for a red team: noncongruence modular forms extending the finite-index-subgroup theory of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms, 'which no roadmap develops further'; the lambda-covering H/Gamma(2) isomorphic to C minus {0,1}, 'planned here because no layer plans it'; arithmetic algebraization, which 'DT.0-DT.5 do not cover'; and a ConformalMapping Part II. These are proposals under review, so filing them would duplicate work already in the queue, exactly as with PAPER-BRESCIANI-24's ProfiniteProPGroups Part II in part 2 of the arithmetic-geometry area.

Library trees, with sizes printed beside every result after two wrong paths produced false cleans earlier in this session: a full Mathlib checkout of 8556 .lean files and the Tau Ceti library tree of 5268.

findings.where: AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.2 (integral q-expansion principle and finite generation), and the atlas as a whole
findings.claim: Shimura's bounded-denominators theorem is stated by no node. R15.2 plans the integral q-expansion principle and the finite generation of spaces of forms, and PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25's route records that the bounded-denominators theorem is the companion statement at every prime, that the R15 decomposition imports it without a node, and that it closes a finite-freeness gap already recorded there for the Deligne-Serre module. A second roadmap records the same absence from its own side: IntegralIwasawaTheory needs the distribution and bounded-denominator theorem for Hilbert modular Eisenstein series and says it must be imported from a verified supplier or implemented as an explicit prerequisite. So a statement that two roadmaps depend on has no owner, and one of them has a recorded gap that it would close.
findings.evidence: The route, PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25 to AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.2: 'R15.2 plans the integral q-expansion principle and the finite generation of spaces of forms. Shimura's bounded-denominators theorem [Shi71, Theorem 3.52] is the companion statement at every prime. The R15 decomposition imports it without a node, and it also closes the finite-freeness gap recorded there for the Deligne-Serre module.' The second, independent record of the absence, in IntegralIwasawaTheory: 'This includes Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences and the distribution/bounded-denominator theorem. These general Hilbert modular constructions must be imported from a verified supplier or implemented as the Iwasawa proof's explicit prerequisite; weight-two quaternionic forms alone do not supply them.' Ownership searches across both roadmap directories: 'bounded denominator' in any spelling returns 2 files and neither states this theorem — HeegnerPointEulerSystems uses 'bounded-denominator derivative classes' and 'bounded-denominator/error estimates' in Kolyvagin's Euler-system sense, and IntegralIwasawaTheory is the roadmap quoted above, which records the need rather than owning it. 'Shi71' returns 0 files. A search for Shimura's Theorem 3.52 returns one file, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms, and reading it shows a different use: it cites 'Shimura Thm 3.48/3.51/3.52; Miyake section 4.5' as source support for its own target that the coefficient field of a newform is a number field, proved through the integral Hecke algebra being a finitely generated Z-module. That is a source citation for another statement, not a node stating bounded denominators, and the instruction there is to 'cite the section, not a single theorem number'.
findings.fix: State the theorem as a node of R15.2, with Shimura's Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions, Theorem 3.52, as its source: for a modular form on a finite-index subgroup whose q-expansion has algebraic coefficients, the denominators of those coefficients are bounded, in the form needed at every prime rather than one prime at a time. R15.2 is the right owner because it already plans the integral q-expansion principle and finite generation, and the route records that this statement closes the finite-freeness gap noted there for the Deligne-Serre module, so the node pays for itself twice. IntegralIwasawaTheory should then cite it as the verified supplier it asks for instead of keeping the Hilbert modular case as an open prerequisite; if the Hilbert case needs more than the classical statement, that difference should be recorded on the new node rather than left to each consumer. Note that tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms cites the neighbouring Shimura theorems for a different purpose, so the node should not be assumed to exist there.
